To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

‘Web-based grassroots initiatives are successful because they provide authentic and relevant learning opportunities for their participants, and they do so by leveraging the social affordances of social software, and the social capital of the participants’.

(1) the social Web is providing a fertile ground for grassroots initiatives to emerge; (2) these initiatives are successful in engaging a vast public in learning and knowledge enhancement; (3) these initiatives are authentic in their engagement of learners; (4) the social Web enables authentic engagement by providing a fertile ground and a set of powerful tools for learning; (5) the social Web provides a fertile ground for learning and knowledge creation because of its characteristics, which include openness, participation, and network
grassroots initiatives for learning are successful when they are authentic and when they are based on the principles of the social Web, such as openness, participation and trust.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how social software is used to support learning in the context of web-based grassroots initiatives.
the following research questions: How can social software support the creation of web-based grassroots initiatives that foster learning and knowledge enhancement through social interaction?
the following questions: What are the key features of web-based grassroots initiatives?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
social software is a powerful tool for learning and knowledge building, but it is not the solution.
social media are a powerful tool for learning, knowledge development and social engagement.

the Web-based grassroots initiatives for informal learning are successful in engaging people in a social and collaborative way, because they are authentic, and because they are able to create a sense of community.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the success of grassroots initiatives for learning is related to the authentic engagement of the community, which is enabled by the social software.
the social Web has provided a new platform for learning, where people can engage in learning and knowledge development through social media, and where the learning experience is authentic.
the social Web is providing new possibilities for learning and knowledge building, but it is also changing the way we understand learning, knowledge and the role of the individual.
The main takeaway from our work is that

social media can be used as tools to support authentic engagement, in which learners are engaged by a topic of interest and are able to contribute in a way that is meaningful to them and to the community of practice.

the social Web can be successfully used for learning and knowledge sharing, if the initiative is authentic, i.e., the initiative is not a mere attempt to use social media for education but it is an authentic engagement, where the social media are used to achieve an authentic purpose.

grassroots initiatives are authentic engagement experiences that are successful in attracting people and keeping them engaged, and that are able to leverage social software to support the development of learning and knowledge.
